![The Apache Hop horse has come a long way (source: Stefan Ziegler)](spatial-horse-1500x1000.jpg "The Apache Hop horse has come a long way (source: Stefan Ziegler)")

News from Apache Hop in the geospatial domain _(Spatial Hop? SHop? SHOP?)_:

At [hop.interlis.guru][shop], [Stefan Ziegler][stefan] has published a new 
Apache Hop version[^os] under the monicker "Spatial tools and plugins for 
Apache Hop" with the tagline "Apache Hop with spatial plugins already included. 
Read, transform and write geospatial data in visual pipelines." This is pretty 
much the most concise description of this new Hop version.

The [announcement post][post] by Stefan has a few more details:

> The geodata import and export functionalities have received a major update: 
[...] a ‘pure Java’ approach using Geotools and my own code. This means I can 
do without the ‘heavy’ OGR/GDAL plugin. [...] 
>
> Naturally, far fewer formats are supported, but the most important ones are
included: Shapefile, GeoPackage and File Geodatabase. For export only,
FlatGeobuf, (Geo-)Parquet and Arc Generate are supported. The most important
format of all (INTERLIS[^interlis]) receives special treatment in the form of a 
dedicated plugin (à la `ili2fme`). Furthermore, with the `ili2db` plugin, you 
can always import or export INTERLIS to and from PostgreSQL and GeoPackage. 
[...]
> 
> The Geometry Inspector is increasingly becoming a Data Inspector. It can now 
display multiple streams and supports an initial form of caching (for some 
transformers).

I wonder how much steam^[Tokens?] is left 
in Stefan's Hop development effort. Two is one and one is none.

In any case: Interesting stuff. The [prepared examples and sample data][ex] 
should help curious people find their footing and test Spatial Hop for their 
workflows.
